10-13.title: Marriage registration in India: the documents and the notice depend on the law you marry under
10-13.inPlainWords: A Hindu marriage can be registered under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955; a marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 needs a notice to the marriage officer and a 30-day window for objections. Documents usually include age proof, address proof, photographs and witnesses. There is no household-register requirement, and no fee should be paid to an agent to 'fix' a date.
10-13.benefit: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (section 8) and the state registration rules govern registration. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 requires a notice and a certificate; the notice is public and allows objections. The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 sets the minimum age at 18 for a woman and 21 for a man. A registrar may ask for proof of age and address, but not a household register. A marriage solemnised under a religious law can be registered under that law.
10-13.cost: The fee is small and set by the state. A lawyer is optional for a straightforward registration. Do not pay an agent for a 'guaranteed' date.
10-13.caveats: A marriage registration is not the same as a marriage; the ceremony and the applicable law come first. A notice under the Special Marriage Act is public, so a person in a hurry may prefer a different route. Keep the certificate safe; it is needed for a passport and a visa.
10-13.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>

10-2.title: Stop after a clear refusal: pursuit against a clear 'no' can be stalking, not persistence
10-2.cost: No money, and no time beyond the messages you stop sending. The hard part is self-restraint: not sending another message, not waiting outside, not asking friends to plead your case.
10-2.inPlainWords: Once someone has clearly said no, further pursuit is not romance. In India, repeatedly following or contacting a woman against her wishes can be stalking under the BNS, 2023, and a threat can be criminal intimidation. Obscene messages fall under the IT Act, 2000, and a court can grant a protection or injunction order. Your intention does not draw the line; the other person's clear refusal does.
10-2.benefit: Section 78 of the BNS, 2023 punishes stalking, which includes following a woman, contacting her repeatedly against her wishes, watching her, and monitoring her use of the internet or email; section 77 covers voyeurism. Threats are criminal intimidation under the BNS, 2023, and obscene electronic messages fall under the IT Act, 2000. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 applies where there is a domestic relationship and can give a protection order. On a campus the UGC sexual-harassment regulations apply, and at a workplace the PoSH Act, 2013. The normal route is a police complaint or an FIR, not an administrative detention.
10-2.caveats: No research shows that persistence wins someone over, and the law does not reward it. A police record can affect a background check, a government job and a professional licence. A false complaint is itself actionable, so keep your own messages and dates. If a refusal is ambiguous, ask once, in writing, and accept the answer.
10-2.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Commission for Women. <https://ncw.nic.in/>

10-7.title: Read the numbers behind 'marriage rate' and 'divorce rate' before you believe a claim about marriage
10-7.cost: Nothing but a few minutes. India has no single national marriage register, so check what a figure actually counts before you repeat it.
10-7.inPlainWords: India does not publish one national count of marriages and divorces. Marriages are registered under state rules made under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the Special Marriage Act, 1954 and the personal laws, while the Registrar General's Civil Registration System covers births and deaths, not marriages. A 'divorce rate' quoted online is often just the number of divorces divided by the number of marriages in the same year. Those are different groups of people, so the ratio is not the chance that a marriage ends.
10-7.benefit: A crude marriage rate divides the number of marriages in a year by the whole population, including children and unmarried people; a divorce-to-marriage ratio divides one year's divorces by that year's marriages. Neither tells you what happens to a given couple. Answering that needs a cohort followed for decades, and India does not publish one. The usable Indian sources are the Civil Registration System reports, the National Family Health Survey and the National Statistical Office surveys; read the definition before the headline.
10-7.caveats: Under-registration and differences between states make a national comparison misleading, and a high ratio can simply reflect many marriages in the past or few marriages this year. Do not use a ratio to predict your own marriage, and do not accept a percentage from a screenshot without the year and the definition.
10-7.sources: Registrar General of India, Civil Registration System. <https://crsorgi.gov.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. <https://www.mospi.gov.in/>

10-9.title: Agree how unpaid work will be shared before marriage: no law will divide it for you afterwards
10-9.cost: No money. Spend an hour or two before marriage agreeing who does the cooking, cleaning, childcare and elder care, and how that changes when a child arrives or a parent falls ill. The hard part is the conversation, not the cost.
10-9.inPlainWords: India's Time Use Survey, 2019, run by the National Statistical Office, found that women spend far more of the day on unpaid domestic work and care-giving than men. The survey did not report the split by marital status, so there is no official figure for how much housework rises after marriage. The law does not divide housework; it matters later, when a court fixes maintenance or when one spouse has given up a career.
10-9.benefit: The Time Use Survey, 2019 measured unpaid domestic services and care-giving separately for men and women and found a large gap; read the report tables rather than a summary. The legal consequences of that gap appear at separation: maintenance and alimony under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954, interim maintenance and litigation expenses, and monetary relief under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. A written household agreement has no statutory force, but it records the intention and can be evidence later.
10-9.caveats: A national average says nothing about your household, and a couple may choose any division they like. What matters is that the arrangement is stated, reviewed when circumstances change, and not assumed. If one partner stops paid work to care for children or parents, record that decision and keep the money arrangements in both names where possible: joint accounts, nominations and property documents.
10-9.sources: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Time Use Survey. <https://www.mospi.gov.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>

10-10.title: Check what Indian law says about money and property in marriage, then decide whether a written agreement helps
10-10.cost: No money to read the rules. A written agreement costs what a lawyer charges, and a registered deed costs stamp duty and registration fees set by the state. The real work is an honest conversation about money before marriage.
10-10.inPlainWords: India has no community of property: nothing says that everything earned during a marriage belongs to both spouses. Property generally belongs to the person in whose name it is held, and a Hindu woman's property is her own absolutely. What marriage does create is maintenance, a right of residence in the shared household, and rights in a joint family's coparcenary property. A written agreement can record intentions, but it cannot sign away maintenance or a child's rights.
10-10.benefit: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 makes a daughter a coparcener (section 6), makes a Hindu woman's property her absolute property (section 14) and lists a widow among Class I heirs (section 8). The Indian Succession Act, 1925 governs wills and the succession of Christians and Parsis, and Muslim succession follows personal law. A marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 takes its succession from the Indian Succession Act. A Hindu marriage is dissolved under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, with maintenance and a share of jointly held property. A prenuptial agreement has no statutory basis in India and courts have taken differing views, so it is evidence of intention, not a substitute for statutory rights.
10-10.caveats: Goa, whose family law comes from the Portuguese era, is the main exception and recognises a form of joint property. A gift from a relative, including a spouse, is generally not taxed as the recipient's income under section 92(3) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, which is the Act in force from 1 April 2026, but a transfer of immovable property needs a registered deed and stamp duty. Keep the title, the payment trail and the loan documents in both names where you want both to own. Do not assume a clause waiving maintenance will be enforced.
10-10.sources: Hindu Succession Act, 1956. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>

10-11.title: When parents pay for a house, say at the time of payment whether the money is a loan or a gift
10-11.cost: No cost for the note itself. A loan agreement or a gift deed costs what a lawyer charges, and a deed for immovable property needs stamp duty and registration. Write it on the day the money moves, not after a dispute.
10-11.inPlainWords: When parents pay for a house, the money can be a gift or a loan, and the difference matters if the marriage later breaks down. A gift to a son or daughter is that child's property, but a house bought in the couple's joint names belongs to both. A loan is repayable to the parents and is proved by the transfer, the agreement and any repayments. Put the choice in writing, sign it, and have both spouses sign if it is a loan.
10-11.benefit: Indian courts look at the source of the funds, the intention of the parents and the conduct of the parties when a house is claimed at divorce, and a document made at the time is far stronger than one produced after separation. A gift from a parent, being a relative, is not treated as the child's income under section 92(3) of the Income-tax Act, 2025. A gift of immovable property needs a registered instrument under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 read with the Registration Act, 1908. For a loan, record the amount, the date, the interest if any and the repayment terms.
10-11.caveats: A document created after the marriage has failed is viewed with suspicion, so date it and keep the bank trail from the parents' account. If the house is in the son's name alone, the wife may still have a right of residence in the shared household under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. If both spouses pay and both names are on the deed, a private note between parent and child cannot undo the title. Take advice before registering anything.
10-11.sources: Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Income-tax Act, 2025. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>

10-12.title: A large loan in your spouse's name is not automatically your debt: check whether you signed or guaranteed it
10-12.cost: No cost. Do not sign as a co-borrower or a guarantor unless you are willing to pay the whole loan, and do not confirm the debt in a message. The hard part is staying calm when a recovery agent calls.
10-12.inPlainWords: In India a debt is yours if you signed the loan agreement, stood as a guarantor, held the account jointly, or mortgaged property you own. A loan in your spouse's name alone is their contract, and a default does not appear on your credit report unless you are a co-borrower. If the loan is secured on a house you jointly own, the lender can enforce the mortgage. Marriage does not make you liable, and silence does not protect you either.
10-12.benefit: The Indian Contract Act, 1872 makes only the parties to a contract liable on it; a surety's liability is co-extensive with the principal debtor's (section 128), and a material variation of the contract without the surety's consent can discharge the surety (section 133). A Hindu undivided family's debt can bind coparceners in limited circumstances, which is one reason to keep business borrowing separate from family property. Where a loan is secured, the lender's remedy is against the mortgaged property under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, whether or not you signed.
10-12.caveats: A joint account, a joint home loan or a co-signed guarantee is the usual way a spouse's debt becomes yours. Check your credit report with each bureau to see which loans name you, and ask the lender for the guarantee document if you are shown as a surety. If a recovery agent threatens you, complain to the lender's grievance officer and to the RBI under its Integrated Ombudsman Scheme. A loan taken for a business you never benefited from is still yours if you signed.
10-12.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>

10-14.title: A premarital health check is voluntary in India: if something serious is found, disclose it before the wedding
10-14.cost: A check-up at a government hospital or health centre is cheap or free; a private panel costs what the laboratory charges. It takes part of a day. The hard part is saying the result out loud.
10-14.inPlainWords: India has no mandatory premarital medical examination and no duty in law to produce a fitness certificate; testing is voluntary. If a serious condition is concealed, the other person's remedy is not an automatic annulment: it depends on the condition and on whether the concealment goes to consent. A marriage can be annulled for impotence, unsoundness of mind, fraud or force, and a marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 can be dissolved for mental disorder or a venereal disease in a communicable form.
10-14.benefit: Sections 11 and 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 deal with void and voidable marriages, and the voidable grounds include impotence, unsoundness of mind at the time of marriage, and fraud or force. Section 13 allows divorce for adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, mental disorder, venereal disease in a communicable form, renunciation and seven years' absence. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 has parallel provisions. Testing itself runs on consent: the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 requires informed consent for an HIV test and protects confidentiality.
10-14.caveats: Doctors and laboratories owe confidentiality, and a result shared with a fiancé is a disclosure the person chooses unless a law requires it. There is no Indian statute that gives a one-year window to annul a marriage for a concealed illness, so do not expect that remedy. If you learn of a serious condition, get medical advice on treatment and transmission and decide together; a court case is slower, costlier and less certain than a conversation.
10-14.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>

10-15.title: Count the cost of leaving before you marry: mutual consent needs a wait, and a contested divorce needs a ground
10-15.cost: Court fees are set by the state and lawyer fees are yours alone; legal aid is free through NALSA if you qualify. The real cost is time: a mutual-consent divorce has a waiting period, and a contested one can run for years.
10-15.inPlainWords: There are two routes. A divorce by mutual consent under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (section 13B) or the Special Marriage Act, 1954 (section 28) needs a joint petition and one year of living apart; under the Divorce Act, 1869 (section 10A) the spouses must have lived apart for two years. In each case there is a second motion after a cooling-off period of six months, which a court can waive. A contested divorce needs a ground such as adultery, cruelty, desertion for two years, conversion, mental disorder or venereal disease. Courts try mediation first.
10-15.benefit: Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 requires the spouses to have lived separately for a year and provides for a decree on a joint petition; in Amardeep Singh v Harveen Kaur (2017) the Supreme Court held that the six-month cooling-off period can be waived where the parties have settled everything. Sections 13 and 13(2) list the contested grounds, including the special grounds available to a wife. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 has its own grounds and a mutual-consent route in section 28 that, like section 13B, requires one year of separation; the Divorce Act, 1869 has its own grounds and a mutual-consent route in section 10A that requires two years. For Muslims, the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 provides grounds, and instant triple talaq is void and an offence under the 2019 Act.
10-15.caveats: Irretrievable breakdown is not a statutory ground in India, although the Supreme Court has dissolved marriages under Article 142 in rare cases. A separation agreement, a waiver of maintenance or a custody clause is not automatically binding if it defeats the child's welfare or a statutory right. Keep the marriage certificate, the separation date and the financial records; they decide which route is open and how long it takes.
10-15.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Divorce Act, 1869. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>

10-18.title: Same-sex partners should sign a will, a power of attorney and a nomination while both are well: Indian law gives a partner no automatic right to decide or to inherit
10-18.cost: A will can be written by hand at no cost; a power of attorney, a nomination with each bank and fund, and a notarised document cost what a lawyer and a notary charge. The set takes a couple of afternoons. The hard part is talking about illness and death.
10-18.inPlainWords: India does not recognise a marriage or a civil union between two people of the same sex, so a partner is not a spouse: not a Class I heir, not a next of kin for a hospital, and not entitled to a family pension. Four documents close most of the gap: a will naming the partner, a power of attorney for money and property, nominations in bank, provident fund and insurance accounts, and a written authority the hospital will accept.
10-18.benefit: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 lets a person leave property by will to anyone, and section 63 requires the will to be signed and attested by two witnesses. A power of attorney under the Powers of Attorney Act, 1882 lets the partner act on property and financial matters, and one dealing with immovable property is normally registered. Nominations under the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme and in insurance policies pay the nominee. The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 allows an advance directive and a nominated representative for mental-health decisions. The Supreme Court recognised a limited form of advance medical directive in Common Cause v Union of India (2018), and declined to recognise same-sex marriage in Supriyo v Union of India (2023).
10-18.caveats: There is no 'voluntary guardianship agreement' in Indian law; the nearest instruments are the will, the power of attorney, the Mental Healthcare Act advance directive and the nomination. Hospitals differ in what they accept at the desk, so ask your regular hospital what it needs and keep a signed letter with the partner's phone number. For organ donation, the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 defines 'near relative' narrowly, so a partner may need the authorisation committee. Review the will after any change in assets or family.
10-18.sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Powers of Attorney Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>

10-19.title: Do not marry while hiding your orientation, and do not treat a marriage of convenience as a short-term arrangement: in law it is a real marriage
10-19.cost: No money to decide honestly. The cost of a marriage entered to satisfy family is years of a life you did not choose, and a divorce at the end of it. The hard part is refusing the pressure now.
10-19.inPlainWords: Indian law does not recognise a marriage between two people of the same sex, and it does not annul a marriage because one spouse is gay or lesbian. Concealment may be argued as fraud or cruelty, but the outcome depends on the court; the reliable exit is divorce. A marriage of convenience is a real marriage: maintenance, property, a child's legitimacy and succession all follow from it, and marrying again while it subsists is bigamy.
10-19.benefit: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954 set the conditions for a valid marriage and the grounds for divorce, and neither list includes sexual orientation. Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act allows annulment for impotence, unsoundness of mind, fraud or force, and a court may treat a fundamental deception about the marriage as fraud, but the case law is not uniform. Maintenance is available under sections 24 and 25 of that Act and under section 144 of the BNSS, 2023. Bigamy is an offence under the BNS, 2023. The Supreme Court decriminalised consensual same-sex sex in Navtej Singh Johar (2018) but declined to recognise same-sex marriage in Supriyo v Union of India (2023).
10-19.caveats: Compensation for emotional distress is not a standard remedy in an Indian divorce; a court may order costs, maintenance and a share of joint property, and may treat the deception as cruelty. A child born of the marriage is legitimate whatever happens to the marriage. If both spouses have partners of their own, those partners get nothing from the marriage, so their property and care arrangements need separate documents.
10-19.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>

10-21.title: A wedding alone can be a valid marriage in India, but register it: without a certificate, proving it costs years
10-21.cost: Registration fees are small and set by the state. A wedding without a certificate costs nothing at the time and a great deal later, when a pension, a succession certificate or a visa needs proof.
10-21.inPlainWords: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 a marriage is complete on the ceremony, and registration is evidence rather than the source of validity; a marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 is different, because the marriage officer solemnises and registers it. If your partner dies and you were never registered, you are still a widow or widower in law, but you must prove the marriage with photographs, invitations, witnesses and joint records, which a pension office, a bank or a court may not accept quickly.
10-21.benefit: Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 sets out the ceremonies and section 8 provides for registration; section 8(5) says the validity of a Hindu marriage is not affected by the omission to register it. The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 makes a widow a Class I heir. For Christians and Parsis the Indian Succession Act, 1925 governs succession, and for Christians the Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872 governs the ceremony. For Muslims the nikah is recorded in the nikahnama under state registration rules. Registration is the cheapest evidence you will ever buy.
10-21.caveats: An unregistered partner is not automatically excluded from inheritance, but every claim becomes a proof problem. Children of a void or voidable marriage are legitimate under section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. A live-in partner is not a spouse: the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can protect a relationship in the nature of marriage, but it does not create inheritance rights. Register while both of you can sign.
10-21.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Succession Act, 1956. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>

10-22.title: If a spouse spends large sums on someone outside the marriage, follow the money: India has no joint property to divide, so the remedy depends on whose name the asset is in
10-22.cost: A lawyer and court fees, and court fees are not recovered from the losing side. Tracing the money takes weeks: bank statements, UPI records, card bills and the platform's statements. Prevention is cheaper: keep one account in your own name and know where the family money sits.
10-22.inPlainWords: Indian law does not treat a couple's earnings as common property, so there is no 'divide the property during the marriage' remedy of the kind some countries have. What you can do depends on the asset: if a house or account is in your name or jointly held, you can sue for a declaration, an injunction or partition; if the spending is draining the family, it is a factor when a court fixes maintenance. Money paid to a fraudster on a livestream can also be reported as cyber fraud.
10-22.benefit: Maintenance and interim relief are available under sections 24 and 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the parallel provisions of the Special Marriage Act, 1954, and under section 144 of the BNSS, 2023; a court can take a spouse's spending and concealment into account when fixing the amount. Section 53 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 lets a creditor challenge a transfer of immovable property made with intent to defeat or delay creditors; it is a creditor's remedy about immovable property, not a general power for a spouse to claw back money spent on a third party. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides monetary relief and compensation. Where the recipient is a fraudster, report it at cybercrime.gov.in or on 1930.
10-22.caveats: A gift to a third party is not automatically recoverable by the other spouse, because the money may never have been the other spouse's property. If the account is joint, the bank's records decide who withdrew what. Collect the statements yourself; a court will not go fishing for you. Do not confront the recipient directly, and do not sign a settlement before you have the numbers.
10-22.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>

10-23.title: When you divorce with young children, put custody, monthly support and the exact visiting days into the decree
10-23.cost: A settlement inside a mutual-consent divorce costs the drafting; a contested custody fight costs years and fees. Court fees are set by the state, and legal aid is free through NALSA if you qualify. The expensive part is vagueness.
10-23.inPlainWords: Custody in India is decided by the child's welfare, not by the parents' wishes, and there is no fixed percentage for monthly support: a court looks at the child's needs, the parents' income and the standard of living. A child under five is ordinarily with the mother. Write the amount, the payment date, the bank account, the handover hours, the holidays and the school fees into the agreement, because enforcing a vague clause means a fresh case.
10-23.benefit: The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 gives the mother custody of a child below five years in the ordinary case, and the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 makes the child's welfare the paramount consideration. Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 lets the court make custody and maintenance orders, and section 144 of the BNSS, 2023 provides a quick maintenance order for a wife and children. A child's own wish is a factor, not a rule tied to a fixed age. Maintenance can be varied when circumstances change.
10-23.caveats: A clause that one parent pays nothing is not the end of the matter: a court can order support later if the child's needs require it, and a waiver of the child's rights is not binding. Visitation is enforced through the court, never by taking the child. The 20 to 30 percent of income figure that circulates online is not a statutory rule in India. Keep receipts for school fees, medical bills and travel, and record every missed visit.
10-23.sources: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
